description.narrative: The proposed project will replace ageing electrical and mechanical equipment for power generation and transmission at the Uch-Kurgan hydropower plant (HPP) in the Naryn River cascade and undertake silt and sedimentation removal which hinders the proper operation of hydromechanical equipment of the HPP. This will (i) increase the availability of clean hydropower for domestic use and potential export to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, (ii) enhance the integrity of hydromechanical structures and, ensure safe and optimal reservoir operation, and (iii) contribute to multiyear water supply management from the Naryn River cascade, which is essential for downstream agriculture mainly in Uzbekistan.

Uch-Kurgan HPP annual electricity generation increased to 1,064 GWh Progress/Status: The project took effect only on 31 Mar 2020. EPC for Package 2 was awarded to CNECC-DFEM at the contract amount of $78,954,500. PIC contract was signed and awarded on 31 March 2021 to JV EDF (Leader), Egis Eau and Egis International amounting to USD$ 3,354,614.70. Rehabilitation of the first unit commenced in March 2024 and completed in December 2024. Rehabilitation of the second unit commenced in March 2025 completed in December 2025. Data Source: EPP Annual Report; Uch Kurgan HPP annual operations reports Actual value:

The contract with the coordinator was signed on 21 October 2025. The draft program is being finalized. Data Source: EPP annual report on personnel and human resources

Output: Uch Kurgan HPP facility modernized Indicator: Uch Kurgan HPP installed capacity increased to 216 MW with at least 40 years economic life Progress/Status: Rehabilitation of the first unit (Unit 4) commenced on 5 March 2024 and completed in December 2024. Rehabilitation of the second unit (Unit 3) commenced on 10 March 2025 and completed in December 2025. Rehabilitation of the two remaining units are expected to commence in February-March 2026 and to complete by the end of December 2026. The key project implementation issues identified include: the suspension of services by the Project Implementation Consultant (PIC) in January 2025 due to ongoing contractual disputes with the EA and the premature exhaustion of the contract budget.
